description: The Gnu, the retired maintainer. He appears only through notes, voicemails and sticky labels. One piece per machine part (shown the first time a player opens that part, before the puzzle's own intro), six notes around town, and the last fortune.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Phrase banks: I always knew which bank fed which printer slot.
I kept it in my head, which is not a filing system. Sorry. - G.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Ink pump: I lettered every tube. I did that much, at least.
If the fortunes print pale, a tube has wandered off. They do that. - G.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Hi, it's me. Did the job list fall off the wall again? The tape never holds.
The machine does it the way you would by hand. Just faster. Oh, my bus. Bye!

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: I dropped the phrase drawer and a fortune came apart. It rhymed once.
Read it out loud. Your ear knows more than you think. - G.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Printer: stamps on the beat. Do not rush it.
(I always rushed it.)

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Seagull has been rescuing my lost fortunes for years.
I never once said thank you. Would you say it for me? - G.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: The batter jars! I took the labels off to wash them, and then I retired.
The recipe is still out there. In bits. On the cookies, mostly. Sorry. - G.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Mixer controller: the colored bands are numbers. Old trick, still good.
Penguin, if you're reading this: you were right about the faded label.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Penguin, it's the gnu. I shuffled your recipe card looking for my glasses.
They were on my head the whole time. The card was not. So sorry about the card.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: I write my maintenance notes in rhyme, so I'll remember them.
I did not remember where I put them. - G.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Press: listen to the belt. Thump when it says thump.
Not before. Not after. (Mostly not after.)

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Penguin knows every gear in that machine better than I ever did.
I just never asked. Don't be like me. Ask Penguin. - G.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: It's me again. Every heat zone wants its own temperature. They're fussy.
I set them by feel for thirty years. Feel doesn't fit on a sticky note. Sorry.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Thermostat: every port has its own sticker. Trust the stickers.
Do not trust my handwriting on the back of them.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Steam shuffles the Oven's stage list every spring. Every spring, I forget.
Follow one cookie, start to finish. That's all the Oven knows how to do. - G.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: The packaging label is a little poem. Gopher liked it. So did I.
The steam got at it. If you can make it rhyme again, it's yours. - G.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Folding arms: a warm cookie bends. A cold one cracks.
You only get a moment. Make it count.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Gopher, it's me. Sorry about the maps. I drew north wherever the teahouse was.
That is not how north works. I know that now. Love to everyone on the pier.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: CLOSED. Gone somewhere warm.
The machines are... well. You'll see. Please be kind to them. - G.
pieces.dev_note: Show on the first tap of the Shop hotspot, before the Shop opens.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Red Panda: my tab is paid up through spring.
Keep the kettle on for whoever comes to fix things. Somebody will. - G.
pieces.dev_note: Pinned on the teahouse noticeboard; show after Red Panda's welcome.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: If you found this: I meant to write a manual. I wrote this note instead.
Sorry. Thirty years goes faster than you'd think. - G.
pieces.dev_note: A note in a bottle washed up by the pier.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: THINGS ONLY I KNOW: too many to list.
THINGS I WROTE DOWN: this list.
(The list is otherwise blank. I see the problem now.)

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: You've reached the fortune shop. Nobody's here right now.
Well. If a machine is running, maybe everybody is. Leave a message!
pieces.dev_note: The shop's answering machine, once the player's crew machine runs.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Three machines that each work are not one line that works.
I did the handoffs between them by hand. Every day. Never wrote it down. - G.
pieces.dev_note: Found in the town when the finale opens; points players to Elephant.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: You figured out what I never wrote down. It's yours now. - G.
pieces.dev_note: The gnu's last fortune, from DESIGN.md, inside the first cookie out of the full line. DESIGN.md prints the dash as an en dash; the data uses a plain hyphen for the ASCII rule.
